title: The 26 Best Latin Albums of 2026 (So Far): Staff Picks
summary: From Trueno's TURR4ZO to Elena Rose's No Quiero Que Se Acabe Este Bendito Verano, see which album takes the No. 1 spot.
contentText:
At the halfway point of 2026, Latin music has continued to expand in thrilling, unpredictable directions — not by moving as one, but by moving everywhere at once. The year’s strongest albums so far reflect an ecosystem in constant motion, where established stars, cult favorites and newer-generation disruptors are all reshaping the conversation in real time. From Mexico to Puerto Rico, Colombia to Argentina, Venezuela to Spain, these records capture a rich and restless moment for a genre field that continues to evolve on its own terms.

What stands out across this year’s staff picks is just how broad the canvas feels. Regional Mexican remains a major creative force, yielding albums that lean into tradition, heartbreak and swagger while also stretching the form in moodier, more experimental directions. Elsewhere, Latin pop continues to make room for intimacy, elegance and melodic precision, while urbano artists are pushing toward bolder, more hybridized terrain — often absorbing rock, electronic, salsa and other textures into the mix.

The 26 albums below speak to that range. On this year’s list, readers will find everything from commanding sets by hitmakers like Fonseca , Maluma , Carín León and Christian Nodal to emotionally resonant singer-songwriter projects from Kany García and Julieta Venegas ; from high-voltage urbano and rap releases by Trueno , Eladio Carrión , Arcángel and Tokischa to tropical detours from Rawayana and Neutro Shorty, and collaborative efforts rooted in pure chemistry, like CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso , Peso Pluma and Tito Double P , Paola Jara and Jessi Uribe and Chino & Nacho .

These are the Latin albums our staff has returned to most in 2026 so far — the ones that sparked debate, inspired repeat listens and left a lasting impression. Scroll on for our picks.
